# Bishow's Code Sounds

Build a Cute Premium Monochrome Music Website for Bishow Gyawali

Create a complete, polished personal music portfolio website for Bishow Gyawali, showcasing two original songs created using Strudel.cc.

The website should feel like a cute, charming, slightly quirky indie artist website, while still maintaining a premium, sophisticated black-and-white visual design.

The key aesthetic is:

Cute, cool, minimal, monochrome, personal, and premium.

It should feel like a small personal digital home for an artist who makes music with code.

Do not make it childish, overly colorful, corporate, or aggressively futuristic.

Artist

Bishow Gyawali

Current tagline direction:

Music made with code.

You may improve the tagline if you have a better, more natural option.

Important Content Rule

The current song titles, descriptions, and genre labels are placeholders from my existing code.

Keep them easy to change.

Do not invent final song titles.

Do not invent personal information about Bishow Gyawali.

Technology

Use only:

HTML
CSS
Vanilla JavaScript

Create:

index.html
style.css
script.js


Do not use React, Next.js, Vue, Angular, Tailwind, Bootstrap, jQuery, or other frameworks.

The website must work locally by opening index.html.

Visual Style

Create a premium black-and-white cute indie aesthetic.

Primary colors:

Near-black
White
Off-white
Soft gray

No colorful gradients.

No excessive neon.

No generic futuristic/cyberpunk aesthetic.

No stock photographs.

No fake album artwork.

Instead, create cute visual elements using HTML/CSS.

Examples:

♡
✦
♪
Tiny dots
Thin lines
Small circles
Minimal waveform shapes
Simple abstract forms
Track numbers
Tiny animated indicators

Use these sparingly.

The design should feel:

cute + cool + sophisticated

rather than childish.

No Artwork Strategy

Because there is no album artwork, intentionally make the absence of artwork part of the design.

Create custom monochrome visual compositions for each track.

For example:

Track 01

Large 01 with a small orbit/circle/waveform.

Track 02

Large 02 with a different arrangement of dots/lines/shapes.

Make these visuals feel like tiny pieces of experimental album art created directly with CSS.

They should be simple enough to load instantly.

Hero

Create a beautiful typographic hero.

Possible direction:

BISHOW GYAWALI

little sounds
made with code ♡

[ listen ↓ ]


Use large typography, generous whitespace, and tiny decorative details.

Do not overwhelm the hero with animation.

Music Experience

Make the music section the main focus.

Present the two tracks as a refined editorial track list.

Each track should include:

Track number
Title
Description
Genre
Year
Play button
Progress bar
Current time
Duration
External audio link
Strudel Code link

Create a custom vanilla-JavaScript audio player.

Only one track should play at a time.

When playing, add a subtle cute animation such as tiny bouncing dots or a minimal waveform.

Strudel

Make the connection to Strudel part of the website identity.

Include:

Made with code ♡

Explain briefly that the music is created using Strudel.

For each track provide:

View Strudel Code ↗

Open the supplied Strudel URL in a new tab.

Never display the encoded Strudel source on this website.

About

Include a short About section for Bishow Gyawali.

Use placeholder copy because a final biography has not been provided.

Do not invent facts.

The writing should be casual, creative, and personal.

Social Section

Create a minimal social-links section containing:

Facebook
Instagram
YouTube
GitHub

Use monochrome text/icon treatments.

Do not use colorful brand buttons.

Responsive Design

Make the website mobile-first and fully responsive.

It should look intentionally designed on:

Mobile
Tablet
Laptop
Desktop

Pay particular attention to the audio player on mobile.

Accessibility

Include:

Semantic HTML
Keyboard navigation
Visible focus states
Good color contrast
Accessible audio controls
Appropriate ARIA labels
Reduced-motion support
Performance

Keep the website extremely lightweight.

Do not use heavy libraries or unnecessary assets.

Do not use WebGL or large particle systems.

Animations should be CSS-based wherever possible.

Code Architecture

Store track information in a JavaScript array so additional tracks can easily be added later.

Use CSS custom properties for the design system.

Keep all social links in one easy-to-find configuration area.

Clearly mark all values that I need to replace.

Final Quality Standard

Before delivering the code, review it as a senior UI/UX designer.

Ask:

Does it actually feel cute?
Does it still feel premium?
Is the black-and-white palette sophisticated?
Does it look good without artwork?
Does the music feel like the main focus?
Are the animations subtle?
Does it feel like a real artist's personal website rather than an AI-generated template?
Is the mobile experience excellent?
Is the audio player intuitive?
Can I easily add more songs later?

If anything feels generic, cluttered, childish, or overly complicated, refine it before presenting the final code.

Then provide the complete:

index.html

style.css

script.js

files, ready to run locally.
